clue.text: Old lady's car without dipstick for oil

parts.note: old lady is slang for mother, giving MA; the 's stands for 'has', joining her to what follows

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the car's letters wrap round the fool

parts.note: taken as written
dipstick is slang for an idiot, an ass

explanation.surface: A mechanic notes that a little old lady's car has no dipstick for checking the oil level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'dipstick' is slang for a fool, not the engine part.
explanation.definitionFit: Macassar is a hair oil popular in Victorian times, named after a port in Indonesia.

clue.text: After game, soldiers in A&E say sorry

indicators.note: in says the game and the soldiers sit inside the hospital letters

parts.note: the letters A and E, as printed

indicators.note: after says the soldiers come later than the game in the string

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers injured after a game turn up at Accident and Emergency and apologise.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British hospital Accident and Emergency department; here it only supplies its two letters as a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To apologise is simply to express regret or say sorry, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Minor charge a result of naughty videotape (no sex)

indicators.note: naughty suggests behaving badly, so the letters of videotape are disordered
no says the letters for sex are left out of the rearranged pool

parts.note: sex is Latin for six, the Roman numeral VI

explanation.surface: A naughty videotape, minus the sex, results in a court charge for a minor.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove VI ('sex', Latin six) from VIDEOTAPE and rearrange the rest ('naughty') to form the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An adopted child is a minor placed in the legal care, or charge, of new parents.

clue.text: The Last Of Us company's gaming platform

indicators.note: the last of picks out the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a company is a team; the 's means 'is', a link to the definition

explanation.surface: Which platform does the company behind the video game The Last Of Us use?
explanation.walkthrough: The Last Of Us is a famous video game, so the title looks like a name, but it is an instruction to take the last letter of 'Us'.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam is the well-known online store and launcher for PC video games.

clue.text: Again accept orders to collect plug

indicators.note: to collect says the instructions gather the advert up inside them

parts.note: a remit is a set of instructions or orders given to someone
a plug is a piece of publicity, an ad

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go and pick up a plug, then is let back in.
explanation.definitionFit: To readmit is to let someone in or accept them once more.

clue.text: Riding behind, guards stop!

indicators.note: guards means the backside surrounds and protects the call to halt

parts.note: behind as a noun is the backside, in British slang the arse
ho is an old call to stop or halt, as in 'whoa'

explanation.surface: A rider at the back of a procession shouts to the guards to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riding behind' looks like the definition; only 'Riding' is.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahorse is an adverb or adjective meaning on horseback, so it fits as riding.

clue.text: A greeting, one they — or he — exchanged

parts.note: one is the indefinite article A

indicators.note: exchanged says these letters swap places to form a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two people exchange a greeting, one of them they and the other he.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanged' shuffles THEYORHE into HOYTHERE, after A from 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor's hail, a traditional call of greeting across the water.

clue.text: Where eggs are produced, everything's the same

definitions.meaning: the female organs that make egg cells
read as 'nothing changes', with nothing as the letter O and changes as a verb meaning differs or alters

explanation.surface: A remark that nothing changes in the place where eggs come from.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: if everything stays the same, then zero (O) is what differs.
explanation.definitionFit: The reproductive glands in women and female animals in which eggs are formed.

clue.text: Why don't we put up a standing stone?

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means written upwards, so read from bottom to top

parts.note: a suggestion; 'let's' says the same thing

explanation.surface: Someone proposes erecting a standing stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A stela is an upright carved stone slab, a monument or marker.

clue.text: Juliet and, ultimately, Romeo, on way of working charm

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after what follows

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a way of working
J is Juliet in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Juliet and Romeo's love works through charm.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo and Juliet are the lovers, but here Juliet is just the NATO letter J.
explanation.definitionFit: Mojo is a magic charm or amulet, and by extension personal magnetism.

clue.text: Returned parcel, held forth, was amplifier

indicators.note: returned means the word is sent back, read from right to left

parts.note: a bale is a bundle or parcel of goods
to hold forth is to speak at length, to orate

explanation.surface: A parcel came back, and someone held forth about the amplifier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was amplifier' is a playful definition: someone who elaborated did the amplifying.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate is to expand on or add detail, to amplify a point.

clue.text: Saw wheels on black floor

indicators.note: on in an across clue means set after the earlier piece

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: wheels as a verb means turns round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a saw is an old saying, a motto

explanation.surface: A saw with wheels is placed on a black floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is not a tool but a proverb, MOTTO, which turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom of a sea or river is its bed or lowest surface.

clue.text: I'll be topless, just fantastic

parts.note: 'Well, I'll be!' is an exclamation of surprise, like 'My!'

indicators.note: topless means losing the first letter

parts.note: just means fair and moral, ethical

explanation.surface: Someone declares they will go topless, which is simply fantastic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fantastic is imaginary, like the stuff of legend.

clue.text: Old Conservative misfit, one moving far left

parts.note: C abbreviates Conservative, the British political party

indicators.note: moving far left says one letter travels to the front of the word

parts.note: a misfit or nonconformist is a deviant
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An old Tory misfit drifts to the far left politically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving far left' sounds political but sends the I of DEVIANT to its front: IDEVANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ci-devant is a French borrowing meaning former, describing someone formerly in a role.

clue.text: US state given private industrial city

parts.note: AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama
given for a while, as a loan: lent
private, belonging to oneself: own

explanation.surface: A US state hands over a private industrial city.
explanation.definitionFit: Allentown is a Pennsylvania city historically known for steel and manufacturing.

clue.text: Jewish sectarian's contribution to limitless energy

indicators.note: contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A member of a Jewish sect contributes to the quest for limitless energy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect of the Second Temple period; the 's reads as 'is'.

clue.text: I contain a fresh flower

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A flower describes itself as containing something fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: A tobacco plant grown in gardens for its fragrant tubular blooms.

clue.text: Withstand — apparently — traitor

parts.note: read as 'with stand': W is the abbreviation for with
apparently says the word is to be read as it appears split, the second half being a stand for paintings

explanation.surface: A defiant traitor seems to hold out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' asks you to split Withstand into W (with) and EASEL (stand).
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel is a sly, treacherous person who betrays others.

clue.text: Secrecy the last resort?

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning sort the letters again

explanation.surface: Keeping things secret is presented as the last resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' reads as re-sort, rearranging THE LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is acting covertly, so as not to be noticed.

clue.text: Reclines with fantasy book in bed

parts.note: a fantasy is an untruth, a lie

indicators.note: in says the book letter sits inside the bed

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed

explanation.surface: Someone reclines in bed reading a fantasy book.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline is to lean back or lie at rest, which is what this phrase describes.

clue.text: One presumably involved in throwing seafood

definitions.meaning: whimsically, someone who lobs things, a thrower
a clawed shellfish eaten as a delicacy

explanation.surface: A person throwing seafood around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presumably' flags the made-up sense: someone who lobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A large marine crustacean prized as food.

clue.text: Put on weight after party, a stone

indicators.note: after places the remaining pieces later than the party

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance party
st is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone gains a stone after a big party.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds, abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: To ballast a ship is to load it with heavy material for stability.

clue.text: Drinker who primarily binges on no good bubbly?

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the following word
bubbly suggests fizzing about, so the letters are mixed up
no says the good letter is left out

explanation.surface: A drinker binges on bad champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no good' drops G from the letters of 'binges on' before 'bubbly' mixes them; 'bubbly' looks like champagne but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretentious connoisseur of vintages is a kind of drinker who sneers at cheap bottles.

clue.text: Cream cakes yellow with poisonous growth

indicators.note: cakes as a verb means coats or encases, so the plant wraps round

parts.note: poison ivy is a toxic climbing plant
or is gold or yellow in heraldry

explanation.surface: Cream-coloured cakes have gone yellow with a poisonous mould.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivory is an off-white, creamy colour.

clue.text: Mineral that is cut by reversing plough

indicators.note: cut by says the ie is split open by the other piece

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: reversing turns the word round, back to front

parts.note: to till is to plough the land

explanation.surface: A plough backs up and cuts into some mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Illite is a clay mineral, a type of mica found in shales.

clue.text: Young ones mostly fat

parts.note: ones as letters, I's, gives IS

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: suet is hard animal fat used in cooking

explanation.surface: Young people are said to be mostly fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young ones' looks like one phrase; split it: ones gives IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring or children, a noun for one's young.

clue.text: Collection points on ring roads?

parts.note: kiosks where payment is collected from drivers; 'ring' hints at the bell sense of toll

explanation.surface: Where money is collected on orbital routes.
explanation.definitionFit: Booths where drivers pay a charge to use a road or bridge.

clue.text: Nurse, a non-professional, in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a ham is an amateur, especially an amateur radio operator or actor

explanation.surface: A nurse, an amateur, has retired.
explanation.definitionFit: An amah is a nursemaid or maid in parts of Asia.

clue.text: Self-employed joiner

parts.note: the dash in the first word is itself a link between two words, not a carpenter

explanation.surface: A freelance carpenter.
explanation.definitionFit: A short dash used to join two words, as in the first word of the clue.

clue.text: Bits of dry grass line choppy waters

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

indicators.note: choppy means rough and broken up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Bits of dry grass float on choppy waters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalks of a cereal crop left after threshing, used for thatching or bedding.
